items.prompt:
Which is a complete sentence?
A) 'The bird flew away.'
B) 'The little bird.'

steps: A has a subject (The bird) and a predicate (flew away). Complete sentence.
B has only a subject and no predicate. Fragment.

items.prompt:
Which is a complete sentence?
A) 'Jumped into the water.'
B) 'The frog jumped into the water.'
items.answer: B) 'The frog jumped into the water.'

steps: A has a predicate but no subject — who jumped? Fragment.
B has a subject (The frog) and a predicate (jumped into the water). Complete sentence.

items.prompt:
Which is a complete sentence?
A) 'The red apple on the table.'
B) 'The red apple sat on the table.'
items.answer: B) 'The red apple sat on the table.'

steps: A is a noun phrase with no verb. Fragment.
B has a subject (The red apple) and a predicate (sat on the table). Complete sentence.

items.prompt:
Which group of words is a complete sentence?
A) 'My older brother and his friends playing basketball.'
B) 'My older brother and his friends play basketball after school.'
items.answer: B) 'My older brother and his friends play basketball after school.'

steps: A uses the verb form 'playing' without a helper verb. Fragment.
B has a subject (My older brother and his friends) and a complete verb (play). Complete sentence.

items.prompt:
Which sentence is most appropriate for a class presentation?
A) 'Yeah, the sun is like, really hot.'
B) 'The sun is an extremely hot star at the center of our solar system.'
items.answer: B) 'The sun is an extremely hot star at the center of our solar system.'

steps: A has informal filler words ('Yeah,' 'like') and vague language ('really hot').
B is a complete sentence using specific, formal vocabulary appropriate for a class presentation.

items.prompt:
Which group of words is a complete sentence?
A) 'Because it was raining outside.'
B) 'We stayed indoors because it was raining outside.'
items.answer: B) 'We stayed indoors because it was raining outside.'

steps: A is a dependent clause — it cannot stand alone as a complete sentence. Fragment.
B has a main subject (We) and a main predicate (stayed indoors), plus the dependent clause. Complete sentence.

items.prompt:
'The tiny spider spinning a web in the corner of the window.'  
What is missing from this sentence? Rewrite it as a complete sentence.
items.answer: Missing: a predicate (a complete verb). The sentence has a subject (The tiny spider) but 'spinning' is a verb form without a helper verb. Rewrite: 'The tiny spider is spinning a web in the corner of the window.'

steps: Subject present: The tiny spider.
'Spinning' is an -ing verb form that needs a helper verb (is, was) to form a complete predicate.
Add the helper verb 'is' to complete the sentence.
Rewrite: 'The tiny spider is spinning a web in the corner of the window.'

items.prompt:
A student presents to the class and says: 'Um, like, I think animals are cool. They are fun.'  
Rewrite the informal parts as formal, complete sentences.
items.answer: Formal rewrite: 'I believe animals are fascinating creatures. They are enjoyable to learn about and observe.' The rewrite removes filler words ('Um, like') and replaces vague words ('cool,' 'fun') with specific, formal language.

steps: Remove filler words: 'Um, like,'.
Replace vague words: 'cool' becomes 'fascinating creatures'; 'fun' becomes 'enjoyable to learn about and observe.'
Both sentences remain complete: subject + predicate in each.
Formal speaking uses specific vocabulary and avoids casual filler words.
